blocks.text: Your day is likely fragmented. You move between grant portals, email, and spreadsheets. Official systems often lack the flexibility you need for specific reporting requirements. This leads to the use of personal spreadsheets to track budgets and deadlines. This shadow work adds up quickly.
Reducing administrative load with your Mac

You can use your Mac more effectively by centralizing your information. When you work in Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace, keep your windows organized. If you use a tool like Instrumentl or Euna Grants, keep those tabs open in a dedicated browser space. Use ⌃ ⌘ F to enter full screen mode to focus on one task at a time.

Email is the biggest drain on your time. You spend 13 hours every week triaging messages. You can improve this by using Apple Mail rules to move incoming grant updates into specific folders. Use the search bar in Mail to find documents by sender or date. If you need to draft a response, hold the fn key to dictate your reply. This keeps your hands on the keyboard and your focus on the content.

Nearly all grant professionals maintain personal spreadsheets. If you use Excel on your Mac, learn the keyboard shortcuts to move faster. Use ⌘ Arrow Keys to jump to the edges of your data. If you get stuck on a function, ask Lazur to point at the menu item you need. This saves time compared to clicking through multiple ribbons.

As a grant administrator, you handle sensitive data. Always follow your employer's rules regarding client or donor information. Do not input protected data into tools that do not meet your organization's security standards. Lazur processes your voice and screen data only while you hold the shortcut. No data is stored for training models.
